title: jev request document
description: A request document for `jev ask --request` and `jev map --request`. This is the official TypeSafe System One evaluation request body (https://docs.typesafe.ai/api), not a format invented by this CLI: a file that validates here is a valid API body for curl or an SDK, and an example copied from the official documentation validates here unchanged. The schema is therefore deliberately NOT versioned by a field inside the document -- adding one would make the file invalid as an API body. It is versioned by its $id, and `jev` accepts exactly the fields the API defines. See docs/commands.md and crates/jev-cli/src/request.rs.

fullDocument.description: A full request document. Recognised when the top level has a `questions` key whose value is an object of question objects.

state.description: What the questions are about. `jev map` ignores this and substitutes each input record.

model.description: The model to evaluate with. Optional; `--model` overrides it, and in `jev map` too. `jev` hard-codes no catalogue -- run `jev models` for the live list. `jev` also caps it at 128 characters *after trimming*, which JSON Schema cannot express -- a plain `maxLength` is measured before trimming, so it red-underlined a padded name `jev` accepts. A schema that rejects a valid file is worse than one that is lax, so the cap is not stated here.

questions.description: Question ids mapped to question definitions. Ids are for your code and are not sent to the model, so the full meaning belongs in `instructions`. Order is preserved. A duplicate id is a load error, not a silent overwrite.

questionId.description: A question id. Also the name a `--require` gate addresses, as `<id>.noul`, `<id>.choice`, `<id>.score`, `<id>.confidence`, or `<id>.probabilities.<key>`. Note that `jev` trims before comparing, so ` a ` and `a` are the same id and the second is a duplicate -- which JSON Schema cannot express, because it sees two distinct property names.

name.description: A non-blank name with no control characters. `minLength` alone is not enough: it does not trim, and `jev` rejects a name that is only whitespace.

noulCriteria.description: Optional guidance for a Noul. Present as an object, it must describe at least one side: `{}` and `{"true": null, "false": null}` are both refused, because they say nothing. A Noul returns the probability that the condition holds and carries no confidence value -- the API returns none and `jev` invents none, so `<id>.confidence` in a `--require` gate is unevaluable. See https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md.

choiceCriteria.description: Each option name mapped to a description, or to null for no description. Include a no-match option when nothing may fit: the model cannot select an option you did not offer. See https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md.

scoreCriteria.description: Ordered level descriptions, lowest first. Each level must describe a concrete situation and stand on its own. See https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md.

content.description: Text, or structured JSON. A null, a boolean, and a bare number are refused: they carry no meaning the model can read. `jev` additionally refuses nesting deeper than 64 levels, which JSON Schema cannot express -- so a very deeply nested document validates here and is still rejected at run time.

nullableContent.description: Content, or null to say there is none.
